newsitem.title: USA: Elk Hills sale on schedule, U.S. Energy Dept says.
newsitem.headline: Elk Hills sale on schedule, U.S. Energy Dept says.

text.p: Preparations to sell the Elk Hills oil reserve in California are proceeding on schedule, U.S. Energy Department officials said Wednesday.
"A huge amount of work has been done in a record period of time," Assistant Energy Secretary Patricia Godley told a House National Security subcommittee.
"I am extremely optimistic we will meet the February 10, 1998 deadline" for the divestiture," Godley said.

Godley said virtually all the steps have been completed to start the formal sales process, and said progress was being made in negotiations with Chevron Corp, which owns a share of the Elk Hills field, to determine the final split in ownership of the field's production.

While Energy Department officials said that sale was moving forward, several congressmen said they still did not know the best course to take with federally-owned Naval Oil Shale Reserves in Colorado and Utah.

Subcommittee Chairman Herbert Bateman, a Virginia Republican, asked the General Accounting Office, Congress' investigative arm, to make a recommendation on whether to sell or lease the reserves that are potential oil and natural gas producers.

Rejecting a consultant's recommendations to sell the reserves, the Energy Department has recommended transferring them to the Interior Department, which would lease them and divide royalty payments for oil and gas production with the states.

The GAO in testimony said there was another option in which the Energy Department would lease the property, and avoid the 50-50 division of royalties with the state because of an exemption in the Minerals Leasing Act of 1920.
